Q: Pillow rendering multiline text for typewriter overlay A:

For that, I had to create a "text wrap" function which returns an array of all text lines, to show the exact position for rendering the latest character or cursor.

def wrap_text(draw: ImageDraw.ImageDraw, text: str, font: ImageFont.FreeTypeFont, max_w: int) -> list[str]:
    """
    Greedy wrap by words to fit max_w pixels. Preserves existing '\n' as hard breaks.
    """
    lines: list[str] = []
    for para in text.split("\n"):
        if not para:
            lines.append("")
            continue
        words = para.split(" ")
        cur = words[0]
        for w in words[1:]:
            trial = cur + " " + w
            if draw.textlength(trial, font=font) <= max_w:
                cur = trial
            else:
                lines.append(cur)
                cur = w
        lines.append(cur)
    return lines

and call it from my render_typewriter_frames

def render_typewriter_frames(
    text: str,
    out_dir: Path,
    *,
    width: int,
    height: int,
    fps: int = 25,
    duration_s: float = 10.0,
    chars_per_s: float = 18.0,
    font_path: str = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf",
    font_size: int = 24,
    margin: int = 30,
    box_height: int = 360,
    line_spacing: int = 12,
):
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    font = ImageFont.truetype(font_path, font_size)

    total_frames = int(duration_s * fps)
    for i in range(total_frames):
        t = i / fps
        n_chars = min(len(text), int(t * chars_per_s))
        reveal = text[:n_chars]

        img = Image.new("RGBA", (width, height), (0, 0, 0, 0))
        d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

        # text box
        # box_top = height - box_height - margin
        d.rounded_rectangle(
             [margin - 30, margin - 30, width - margin + 30, height - margin + 30],
            radius=24,
            fill=(0, 0, 0, 140),
        )

        # wrap revealed text to fit the box width
        max_text_w = (width - 2 * margin)
        lines = wrap_text(d, reveal, font, max_text_w)

        # render lines
        y = margin
        ascent, descent = font.getmetrics()
        line_h = ascent + descent + line_spacing

        for line in lines:
            d.text((margin, y), line, font=font, fill=(255, 255, 255, 255))
            y += line_h

        # cursor: end of last visible line (while typing)
        if n_chars < len(text) and (int(t * 2) % 2 == 0):
            last_line = lines[-1] if lines else ""
            cx = margin + d.textlength(last_line, font=font) + 2
            cy = margin + line_h * (len(lines) - 1)

            d.text((cx, cy), "|", font=font, fill=(255, 255, 255, 255))

        img.save(out_dir / f"tw_{i:05d}.png")

I thought it would be better to call wrap_text once before the frames loop, remember the last line, then just draw / measure lines up to the latest for each frame, but apparently that does not allow for varying overlay dimension, font sizes, font boxes, etc, although it could work if the text input contained "\n"s and every other measurement was constant.

So this is a working solution for a typewriter effect overlay for ffmpeg.

Q: How to check variable for LOW-VALUE/SPACES from DEPENDING ON? A:

Why are you trying to check beyond the range of the DEPENDING ON variable? Change your UNTIL clause.

           PERFORM WITH TEST BEFORE
             UNTIL IND-TEMP-ELEM > OCC-VAL
                OR TEMP-ELEM (IND-TABLE-OCC, IND-TEMP-ELEM) = ORIGINAL-TEMP-ELEM
                OR TEMP-ELEM (IND-TABLE-OCC, IND-TEMP-ELEM) = SPACES
              ADD 1 TO IND-TEMP-ELEM
           END-PERFORM

If range checking was turned on I would expect a detected error for a subscript greater than the number of currently defined elements.

Q: How to solve this simple jQuery issue? A:

Another thought, why take two steps? jQuery is chainable. The return value of a jQuery function is the jQuery object.

$("input").addClass("listenToField").keydown(function () { alert("Hi There"); });

Don't go too overboard with this. When jQuery chains get too long, they become difficult to read.

Q: How to execute bitwise operators in Brainfuck? A:

I wrote the winning answer for the question you got referred to in a comment. You'll notice that that one wants roughly 30 free space to the right. A similar approach could work with more like 18 or 20 space, but 5 space (or 7 in total) is really cramped for this kind of thing. That'll force you to extract only one bit at a time, and it probably makes your code longer and maybe also slower. (Note that all the people who generated brainfuck from another language so far have produced really bloated code.)

As a start point for what you want to do, though, have a look at this code I wrote for asm2bf.

1[l+1-]2[1+n+2-]1[2+1-]e+l[>>[-[->>+<]<]<[>>>+<<]<[-[->>+<]<]>>[>-<<]>>[+[--<<<e[d+1+e-]o]]p[l+p-]e[<+>-]<[>++<-]>l]n[-]e[-] (AND)

1[l+1-]2[1+n+2-]1[2+1-]e+l[>>[-[->>+<]<]<[>>>+<<]<[-[->>+<]<]>>[>-<<]>>+[<<<e[d+1+e-]o[-]]p[l+p-]e[<+>-]<[>++<-]>l]n[e[d+1+e-]d[>+<-]n-]e[-] (OR)

1[l+1-]2[1+n+2-]1[2+1-]e+l[>>[-[->>+<]<]<[>>>-<<]<[-[->>+<]<]>>[>-<<]>>+[<<<e[d+1+e-]o+[-]]p[l+p-]e[<+>-]<[>++<-]>l]n[e[d+1+e-]d[>+<-]n-]e[-] (XOR)

In this, letters and numbers mean to move the pointer to that cell; cells "1" and "2" hold the operands initially, cells "d" and "e" are consecutive, and cells "k", "l", "m", "n", "o", "p" are consecutive. So that's ten cells used; this one replaces operand "1" with the result.

Obvious ways to save cells are: use a bit-extraction algorithm that only wants one navigational zero and not two; reuse a zero from that chunk in place of cell "d"; don't save operand "2" (maybe reuse that space for "e" or something). This could get you down to seven. But you see what I mean about the lack of space.

Q: How to formally verifiy C functions returning pointer types? A:

Regarding your first example, the warning has nothing to do with the failure to discharge the proof obligation: it merely indicates that because you don't say where the value of the pointer returned comes from, Wp's alias analysis might produce wrong separation hypotheses. You can modify your assigns clause this way: assigns \result \from \nothing;. As for why the ensures is not proved, this is because by default Wp does not export in the proof obligations the content of the string literals, as it tends to clutter the formula with a lot of equalities so that provers cannot find their way across the search space. Use option -wp-literals to enable them.

For your second example, Wp basically does not work with dynamic allocation yet, and you won't be able to prove the annotations generated by RTE, even though -wp-literals should allow you to discharge the ensures clause.

Q: How to count word frequencies from an input file? A:

This is a common pattern and core programming skill. You should try collecting and counting words each time you encounter them, in a dictionary. I'll give you the idea, but it's best you practise the exact implementation yourself. Happy hacking!

(Also recommend the "pretty print" python built-in method)

import pprint
for word in file:
    word_dict[word] += 1
pprint.pprint(word_dict)

A couple of extra tips - you may want to f.close() your file when you're finished, (E: I misread so disregard the rest...) and it looks like you want to look at converting your words to lower case so that different capitalisations aren't counted seperately. There are python built in methods to do this you can find by searching

Q: Placing a Legend Title Above a Horizontal Legend Already Positioned at the Top of a Barplot ggplot A:

If you switch to guides(fill = ...) you should be able do it.

Try:

guides(fill = guide_legend(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))

(thanks to @teunbrand, for minor correction)
